scenes.vo: Starbucks is sitting on nearly two billion dollars of customers' own money — interest free.

visual.sub:
SITTING IN CUSTOMERS' MONEY
— INTEREST FREE

scenes.vo: Load money onto the app, and it's a liability on Starbucks' books, not revenue, until you spend it.

visual.headline:
YOUR MONEY,
THEIR LIABILITY

items.text: You load cash onto the app
It sits on Starbucks' books until spent

visual.source: Source: Starbucks 10-Q, stored value card liability

scenes.vo: But some of it never gets spent. Accounting rules let Starbucks count a slice of that as pure profit.
In twenty twenty one, that alone added twelve cents to earnings per share — bigger than Starbucks' whole beat over Wall Street.

visual.sub:
FROM BREAKAGE ALONE — BIGGER
THAN THE EARNINGS BEAT

scenes.vo: A labor federation asked regulators to check Starbucks' disclosures about profit from money people never spend.

visual.sub:
LABOR GROUP TO REGULATORS,
ON BREAKAGE PROFIT

scenes.vo: Starbucks said it only counts gift card cash as revenue once you spend it, and had no further comment.

visual.sub:
COUNTS CASH ONLY WHEN
A CUSTOMER SPENDS IT

scenes.vo: When a company lets you prepay onto an app, it gets a free loan — and keeps whatever you forget to spend.

visual.display: When a company lets you prepay onto an app, it gets a *free* *loan* — and keeps whatever you forget to *spend.*
